newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tanker chartering slows, rates dip.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tanker chartering slows, rates dip.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the key Middle East Gulf slowed on Thursday after moderate activity earlier in the week.
Brokers said that rates on two of the main routes out of the region had dropped fractionally.
VLCCs bound for Japan were fixed at last done levels of W64. Western voyages commanded W53, a drop from Wednesday's W57, whilst rates for VLCCs travelling east descended to W60.
"The tension within the Middle East at the moment is partially responsible for the poor fixing activity," a broker said.
"Despite the fact that 'war insurance' is available, most charterers don't wish to possibly go through the (bother) of losing a vessel and its cargo," a broker said.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med descended to W92.5, although as high as W96.25 was seen done with ERG's chartering of the Raya.
In the inter-UKC sector, rates were seen a touch softer at W95 as evidenced by Conoco's chartering of the Glenross travelling Tees-Tetney.
A single transatlantic charter was seen on the Venitian, a LR2 142,000 tonne vessel, fixed by Statoil.
Caribbean rates remained around last done levels.
Brokers said 70,000 tonners heading up the U.S coast were fixed around W130.
